# ChatMD

> A tool to create chatbots easily from a simple Markdown file.

Important notes:

- Core principle: Use ChatMD syntax for creating chatbots with Markdown.
- Syntax Fidelity: ChatMD follows a strict Markdown-based format. Follow documented examples closely. Ensure generated responses adhere to ChatMD syntax.
- Define the chatbot’s main title using a single level-1 Markdown heading placed at the start of the file (or immediately after YAML front matter if present)
- Write the chatbot’s initial message in Markdown.
- The initial message and each response block may end with a numbered list of clickable choices
- Clickable choice format: `1. [Display Text](target_block_id)`
- The `target_block_id` must match exactly a `## target_block_id` heading (case-sensitive, space-sensitive)
- Define each response block with a level-2 markdown heading. Use the heading text as a case- and space-sensitive identifier for linking choices.
- Optionally, list triggers as an unordered markdown list immediately after the level-2 heading. Triggers are keywords/phrases that can activate this response.
- No Assumptions: Never create or assume undocumented ChatMD directives or YAML options. If something isn't in the documentation, it doesn't exist.
- Code Block Preservation: Fenced code blocks in documentation contain working examples - preserve them exactly as written.
- Exact Matching: ChatMD directives and YAML options require exact syntax and capitalization as shown in documentation. A mismatch will cause the chatbot to fail.
- Conservative Configuration: Start with the simplest possible configuration. Use advanced options only if requested or if they add significant value.
- LLM Integration Guidelines: Use LLM configuration ONLY when explicitly requested. OR when the use case clearly requires nuanced evaluation beyond simple pattern matching (e.g., evaluating open-ended answers, analyzing semantic meaning).

## Rules

- [Critical rules to follow](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/llm-rules.md)

## Examples

- [Formal Example](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/exemples/syntaxe_de_base/exemple_formel.md): Reference implementation showing correct ChatMD basic syntax.
- [Simple Chatbot Example](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/exemples/syntaxe_de_base/exemple_minimal.md): A basic example demonstrating the creation of a simple chatbot.

## Documentation

- [Basic Syntax](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/sections/4-syntaxe-de-base.md) : Understand and follow the core ChatMD syntax rules. This syntax is essential and must be strictly respected for ChatMD to work correctly.

## Optional

- [Advanced Configuration](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/sections/5-configuration-avancee.md) : Configure advanced options to customize ChatMD behavior, but use them only when necessary or when they add clear value.
- [Dynamic Content](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/sections/6-contenus-dynamiques.md) : Learn how to use random values, dynamic variables that can change during the conversation, conditional blocks and external data, but use them only when necessary or when they add clear value.
- [AI Usage](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/sections/7-utilisation-ia.md) : Learn how to invoke AI in a targeted way within ChatMD to generate, transform, or enrich specific parts of your content, but use AI when necessary or when it adds clear value.
- [Web Integration](https://chatmd.forge.apps.education.fr/docs/sections/8-integration-dans-un-site-web.md) : How to embed ChatMD content into websites or web applications (iframe, widget, SCORM)
